title: 5 Blockchains coming for XRP (In Payments)
description:
XRP has real competition and most investors aren't watching the right chains.

1️⃣ ETHEREUM L2s / BASE — Not Ethereum mainnet. Base is quietly absorbing US regulated stablecoin rails through USDC and Coinbase's distribution network. This is the domestic corridor Ripple needs — and it's being claimed while everyone argues about gas fees on a chain that isn't even the threat.
 
2️⃣ STELLAR (XLM) — Circle partnership, active remittance corridors in Africa and Southeast Asia, and a MoneyGram relationship that still matters. Structurally the most similar competitor XRPL has, directly contesting the same market with live infrastructure.
 
3️⃣ LIGHTNING NETWORK — Technically inferior to XRPL in almost every dimension. Still winning corridors XRPL should own through Strike, Cash App, and real merchant integration in El Salvador and the Philippines. Bitcoin being categorically settled as a commodity changes the regulatory calculus in Lightning's favor.
 
4️⃣ SOLANA PAY — Doing real merchant volume in small dollar consumer transactions where XRPL hasn't shown up. Throughput isn't the threat. Consumer distribution is.
 
5️⃣ FLARE NETWORK — The one I keep flipping on. Flare and XRPL are converging on the same institutional data and tokenization use cases. Unlike every other chain on this list, Flare isn't attacking from an adjacent market. It's competing directly for the same use cases on XRPL's home turf.
 
Hot take. Tell me what I'm getting wrong in the comments.
 
This isn't a price prediction video. This is a corridor analysis. I'm breaking down the 5 blockchains actively building in the same payment rails, stablecoin distribution, and remittance lanes that XRPL is targeting — and being honest about where XRP is winning, where it's losing ground, and where the threat is more serious than the community wants to admit.

As an Enrolled Agent (EA) and dedicated content creator since 2018, I provide high-level analysis on the intersection of traditional finance and Web3. My coverage focuses on:
